praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A principal tells a family that their child with multiple disabilities cannot attend the neighborhood school because staff “aren’t trained for that level of need.” What does IDEA require of the district?

options.a: Provide FAPE in the public system; severity does not justify refusing enrollment
options.b: Place the child on a waitlist until a specialist is hired the following year
options.c: Require the family to privately fund a one-to-one aide as a condition of enrollment
options.d: Limit the child to a shortened day until an IEP team later happens to meet

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: IDEA’s FAPE and zero-reject duties apply to every eligible child. A district may not refuse enrollment because staff feel unprepared or the disability is severe; it must serve the child and arrange training, supports, and an IEP. Placement is an IEP-team decision along the LRE continuum, not a principal’s gatekeeping call.

distractorExplanations.b: Waitlisting eligible children postpones FAPE; Child Find and service timelines still run.
distractorExplanations.c: Parents cannot be billed as a condition of public enrollment; FAPE is at public expense.
distractorExplanations.d: A shortened day is a placement/FAPE change the IEP team must justify, not an enrollment stall.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: An IEP lists related services but the annual goals keep a capable student on busywork far below demonstrated skills. Parents argue this is not FAPE. Which standard should guide the team?

options.a: Any signed IEP that names hours of service automatically satisfies FAPE
options.b: FAPE requires the most advanced course sequence the high school offers
options.c: The IEP must be reasonably calculated to enable appropriate progress
options.d: FAPE is met if the student is physically present in a public building

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Endrew F. (building on Rowley) requires an IEP reasonably calculated to enable progress appropriate in light of the child’s circumstances—not mere occupancy or token worksheets. Service minutes on a page do not replace ambitious, individualized goals and instruction.

distractorExplanations.a: Hours listed without meaningful goals can still deny FAPE; paperwork is not the standard.
distractorExplanations.b: FAPE is individualized appropriate progress, not a right to the district’s hardest courses.
distractorExplanations.d: Physical presence without instruction (warehousing) does not meet the FAPE progress standard.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A middle schooler with ADHD meets grade-level standards with extra time, preferential seating, and a quiet testing space, but does not need specialized instruction. Which plan fits?

options.a: An IEP, because ADHD is listed among IDEA’s disability categories
options.b: No written plan, because passing grades bar disability-related supports
options.c: Gifted programming in place of any access accommodations at school
options.d: A Section 504 plan for access accommodations without special education

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: IDEA eligibility requires a listed disability that adversely affects educational performance and a need for specially designed instruction. A student who needs only access supports may be protected under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act even without an IEP. 504 plans commonly document testing and classroom accommodations.

distractorExplanations.a: Category membership is not enough; IDEA also requires need for specially designed instruction.
distractorExplanations.b: Passing grades do not cancel 504 if a disability substantially limits a major life activity.
distractorExplanations.c: Gifted services address high ability; they do not replace 504 access accommodations for ADHD.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A parentally placed private-school kindergartner in the district shows delayed speech. The parent has not asked for testing. What is the public district’s Child Find duty?

options.a: Identify, locate, and evaluate the child even without a parent request
options.b: Wait until the private-school principal files a formal written complaint
options.c: Evaluate only after the child transfers into a public-school classroom
options.d: Limit Child Find to pupils already failing two or more academic subjects

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Child Find is an affirmative duty: LEAs must identify, locate, and evaluate children who may need special education, including parentally placed private-school children in the district where the private school is located. The duty does not wait for a parent letter, a complaint, public enrollment, or failing grades.

distractorExplanations.b: Child Find is the district’s proactive obligation, not a complaint-driven private-school process.
distractorExplanations.c: Private-school children in the district are covered; public enrollment is not a prerequisite.
distractorExplanations.d: Suspicion of disability, not a two-class failure rule, triggers Child Find from birth through 21.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: After a weapons incident, a student with an emotional disability faces a long-term disciplinary removal. What does the zero-reject principle still require?

options.a: Immediate expulsion with a complete cutoff of educational services
options.b: Continued FAPE, including services during a disciplinary change of placement
options.c: Shift tutoring costs to the family for the duration of the disciplinary removal
options.d: Ending the IEP because the conduct is also a criminal offense

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Zero reject means no eligible child is denied public education because of disability severity or behavior. Even after a disciplinary change of placement, IDEA requires continued FAPE—typically services that enable progress on IEP goals and participation in the general curriculum, plus a manifestation determination when timelines are met.

distractorExplanations.a: Long-term removal does not erase FAPE; services continue in an interim alternative setting.
distractorExplanations.c: FAPE remains a public-expense duty; families are not billed as a condition of services.
distractorExplanations.d: Criminal charges do not terminate IDEA eligibility or the IEP’s service obligation.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: Parents receive prior written notice that the district proposes changing their child’s eligibility. Which additional document must explain consent, due process, and dispute-resolution rights?

options.a: The student handbook’s grading scale and homework rules
options.b: A roster of which teachers they may personally select next year
options.c: The IDEA procedural safeguards notice of parental rights
options.d: A brochure describing athletic eligibility and tryout dates

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: IDEA requires that parents receive a procedural safeguards notice explaining rights such as consent, access to records, independent evaluation, mediation, due process, and state complaints. Prior written notice explains a specific proposal; the safeguards notice is the broader rights document, typically provided at key points including eligibility changes.

distractorExplanations.a: Grading and homework policies are general school rules, not IDEA procedural safeguards.
distractorExplanations.b: Parents participate in placement decisions; they do not get to pick a specific teacher by right.
distractorExplanations.d: Athletics flyers are unrelated to consent, due process, and special education dispute rights.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: Parents believe the district denied FAPE by refusing their request for an independent educational evaluation. Which process is designed for this kind of disagreement?

options.a: Appealing a single homework grade to the department chair
options.b: Filing a dress-code complaint with the student council
options.c: Requesting a different homeroom teacher for personality fit
options.d: Requesting an IDEA due process hearing on evaluation and FAPE

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Due process hearings resolve disputes about identification, evaluation (including IEE), educational placement, and FAPE. An IEE disagreement is a classic evaluation/FAPE issue. Ordinary grading, dress code, and teacher-assignment complaints are administrative matters, not IDEA hearing issues.

distractorExplanations.a: A single assignment grade is not an identification, evaluation, placement, or FAPE dispute.
distractorExplanations.b: Schoolwide conduct rules for all students are not IDEA due process subject matter.
distractorExplanations.c: Homeroom teacher assignment is an administrative decision, not a FAPE hearing issue.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A student with a learning disability can access grade-level content with co-teaching and a few accommodations. The team is choosing placement. What does LRE require?

options.a: Educate with nondisabled peers to the maximum extent appropriate
options.b: Start in a self-contained room to prove inclusion is possible later
options.c: Use a separate school whenever the IEP lists specialized instruction
options.d: Remove from general class whenever a standardized score is below average

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Least restrictive environment means children with disabilities are educated with nondisabled peers to the maximum extent appropriate, with supplementary aids and services. Removal occurs only when education in general classes cannot be achieved satisfactorily even with supports. Co-teaching plus accommodations is a typical LRE-first placement for many students with LD.

distractorExplanations.b: LRE is not a “restrict first, include later” ladder; start with the general class plus supports.
distractorExplanations.c: Specially designed instruction can occur in general education; it does not force a separate school.
distractorExplanations.d: A below-average score is not, by itself, a justification for removing the student from peers.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A general education teacher says she need not attend the IEP meeting because “special education owns the paperwork.” What is the correct collaborative practice?

options.a: Let the special educator write the whole IEP without general-ed input
options.b: Hold the meeting after hours with administrators as the only attendees
options.c: Include the general educator as a required IEP team member
options.d: Email the finished IEP after signatures so the teacher can read it

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: IDEA names the general education teacher as a required IEP team member when the child is or may be in general education. Collaboration is not optional paperwork ownership: the general educator contributes present-levels, accommodations, and how the child accesses the general curriculum. Decisions are made at the meeting, not after the fact.

distractorExplanations.a: Solo drafting by special education omits required general-curriculum expertise and team process.
distractorExplanations.b: Administrators cannot substitute for the required parent, special educator, and general educator.
distractorExplanations.d: After-the-fact email is notice, not participation; the teacher must help develop the IEP.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A classroom volunteer asks to photocopy a student’s IEP to “tutor more effectively.” Parents have not consented, and the volunteer is not a designated school official. What should the teacher do?

options.a: Provide the IEP copy because classroom helpers automatically qualify as officials
options.b: Summarize the disability and goals in the weekly class newsletter for families
options.c: Leave the IEP folder on the desk so after-school helpers can read it freely
options.d: Decline the copy; FERPA protects PII without consent or official access

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: FERPA protects personally identifiable information in education records, including IEPs. Disclosure generally requires parent (or eligible student) consent unless an exception applies, such as a school official with a legitimate educational interest under district policy. An informal volunteer without that designation does not get an IEP copy.

distractorExplanations.a: Volunteer status does not automatically create school-official access to education records.
distractorExplanations.b: Publishing disability details is a disclosure to the community, not a FERPA exception.
distractorExplanations.c: Open-desk access is an unauthorized disclosure even if the helper “might need it.”

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A new special educator is told to use a physical restraint she has not been trained to perform because a student is refusing independent work. What is the ethical action?

options.a: Decline untrained restraint and follow the BIP and de-escalation training
options.b: Use the hold once so colleagues see she is willing to be a team player
options.c: Tell classmates the student’s diagnosis so they will ignore the outburst
options.d: Skip a missed IEP service this week because an administrator asked her to wait

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: CEC ethics and typical state restraint rules treat physical restraint as a last resort for imminent danger, used only by trained staff. Work refusal is not an emergency justifying an untrained hold. The teacher maintains competence, follows the BIP, protects confidentiality, and still delivers IEP services rather than deferring them silently.

distractorExplanations.b: Peer pressure does not authorize an untrained restraint for non-dangerous work refusal.
distractorExplanations.c: Sharing a diagnosis with classmates is a confidentiality and FERPA ethics breach.
distractorExplanations.d: Advocacy includes delivering IEP services; administrative convenience does not pause FAPE.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: The speech-language pathologist who serves a student on the IEP asks to review evaluation data needed to write therapy goals. How should FERPA treat this request?

options.a: Deny access because only parents may ever see education records
options.b: Allow access; the SLP has a legitimate educational interest
options.c: Require a fresh parent signature for every related-service contact each week
options.d: Release the full cumulative file to any staff member who emails a request

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: FERPA allows school officials with a legitimate educational interest to access records needed to serve the student. An IEP-assigned SLP reviewing evaluations to plan therapy meets that test. Access is still limited to need-to-know information under district policy—not a blanket “anyone on staff” or a weekly re-consent ritual.

distractorExplanations.a: Parents have access rights, but qualifying school officials may also access records to serve the child.
distractorExplanations.c: Related-service providers on the IEP do not need weekly new consent for ordinary educational access.
distractorExplanations.d: Curiosity or an email request is not a legitimate educational interest for the entire cumulative file.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A student with diabetes needs a nurse-supervised insulin schedule and extra snacks at school but does not require specially designed instruction. Which legal tool fits this need?

options.a: An IEP, because any medical diagnosis automatically triggers IDEA
options.b: No written plan if the student continues to earn passing report-card grades
options.c: A Section 504 plan for health-related access supports at school
options.d: Private nursing paid entirely by the family as a condition of attendance

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Section 504 covers students whose disabilities substantially limit a major life activity (here, endocrine function/health) and who need equal access, even when they do not need special education. Health plans and 504 accommodations (nurse access, snacks, makeup work after medical care) are typical. IDEA requires adverse educational impact plus specialized instruction.

distractorExplanations.a: A diagnosis alone does not create IDEA eligibility without need for specialized instruction.
distractorExplanations.b: Passing grades do not erase 504 duties when a health impairment limits a major life activity.
distractorExplanations.d: FAPE-like 504 access is not conditioned on the family privately funding nursing at school.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: A paraeducator is newly assigned to run a discrete-trial program written by the special educator. What is the best collaborative practice?

options.a: Hand over a binder and leave without modeling, feedback, or data checks
options.b: Let the para rewrite IEP goals if the student appears bored that week
options.c: Ask the para to choose the student’s placement without the IEP team
options.d: Train, model, and supervise the para on the program procedures and data

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: Paras implement instruction under a certified teacher’s direction; they are not independent IEP authors or placement decision-makers. Ethical collaboration includes training, modeling, fidelity checks, and ongoing supervision so the IEP is delivered as written. Dropping a binder without support is neither instructional leadership nor student advocacy.

distractorExplanations.a: Unsupervised binder drop-off leaves the para untrained and the IEP without fidelity monitoring.
distractorExplanations.b: IEP goals are team documents; a para cannot revise them based on weekly boredom.
distractorExplanations.c: Placement is an IEP-team decision; assigning it to a para exceeds the para’s role.

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.prompt: Parents and the district disagree on placement. The district offers mediation. Which statement about IDEA mediation is accurate?

options.a: Mediation is binding arbitration that parents must accept before a hearing
options.b: Mediation is voluntary facilitated negotiation and does not replace hearing rights
options.c: Mediation is an impartial officer taking testimony and issuing a written decision
options.d: Parents must finish mediation before they are allowed to file due process

praxis-special-education-readiness-check.explanation: IDEA mediation is a voluntary, confidential process with a qualified mediator to help parties reach a written, signed agreement. It is not mandatory, not arbitration, and not a hearing. Parents may still file due process; a resolution session (after a complaint) is the step that is generally required, not mediation.

distractorExplanations.a: Mediation is voluntary and nonbinding unless the parties sign a settlement; it is not compelled arbitration.
distractorExplanations.c: Testimony plus a written decision describes a due process hearing, not mediation.
distractorExplanations.d: Mediation cannot be required as a precondition to filing a due process complaint.
